purpose: Give each portfolio job one deterministic create-if-absent collision point per attempt generation while allowing fast evidence-based recovery from silent workers. Explicit multi-party contention fixtures may opt into a timing-only rendezvous barrier before the unchanged deterministic pin race.
authority_boundary: A portfolio pin grants only the bounded candidate execution authority already declared by the selected seed/derived job. It never grants Current, Human Accepted, Served or production /w authority. Collision receipts, heartbeats, barrier entrants, RELEASE and timeout receipts never grant product or execution authority.
winner_rule: For a claimable generation, every contender atomically CREATEs the exact same pin path. Exactly one create may succeed. Only that pin owner may create the authoritative claim receipt and begin substantive work. A create-exists/CAS-lost result means race lost: record collision evidence and immediately re-enter allocation.

contention_barrier_mode.activation: Barrier/rendezvous behavior is enabled only for an explicit multi-party contention fixture whose durable job/fixture metadata names a contention barrier. If no explicit barrier is named, workers follow the normal direct deterministic pin race with no wait or rendezvous step.
contention_barrier_mode.scope: Timing coordination for deliberate multi-worker contention canaries only; it is not a general allocator lock, queue, lease or authority primitive.
contention_barrier_mode.barrier_config: BARRIER.json is immutable timing evidence declaring fixture_id, required_contenders, opened_at and deadline_at before entrants register.
contention_barrier_mode.registration: Each distinct worker atomically CREATEs one append-only entrant receipt keyed by worker_id. Duplicate registration by the same worker is idempotent and never increases quorum.
contention_barrier_mode.pre_release_rule: Before a valid RELEASE exists, entrants MUST NOT attempt the portfolio pin for that fixture. They may emit liveness evidence while waiting, but the entrant receipt grants no execution authority.
contention_barrier_mode.release_predicate: RELEASE is eligible only while observed_at is strictly before deadline_at and distinct entrant worker_ids >= required_contenders.
contention_barrier_mode.release_race: Eligible entrants may race atomic CREATE of the single deterministic RELEASE.json. Exactly one create wins; create-exists readers consume the same append-only release evidence.
contention_barrier_mode.release_authority: RELEASE coordinates start timing only and MUST declare grants_execution_authority=false. After RELEASE, every entrant still races the exact PORTFOLIO_PIN_PROTOCOL deterministic generation path. Only the pin winner may create the execution claim.
contention_barrier_mode.loser_rule: A released entrant that loses the pin race creates no execution claim, records the normal portfolio pin collision receipt when possible, then re-enters allocation.
contention_barrier_mode.timeout: If deadline_at is reached without RELEASE, the entrant writes an append-only timeout receipt with pin_attempted=false and next_action=REENTER_ALLOCATION. It MUST NOT attempt the portfolio pin for that fixture.
contention_barrier_mode.late_release: A barrier that reaches deadline without RELEASE cannot release later merely because quorum arrives after the deadline. A fresh fixture/barrier generation is required.
contention_barrier_mode.normal_job_compatibility: Ordinary portfolio jobs are unchanged and never wait for barrier quorum unless explicit durable barrier metadata opts them in.

post_claim_start_signal.rule: STARTED is the canonical primary post-claim signal. If STARTED persistence is blocked only after a deterministic PIN has already been created, the PIN remains authority. Before substantive mutation the owner may create the exact worker/job heartbeat fallback above. That heartbeat is durable liveness consumed by Live but grants no execution authority. If neither signal can be persisted, perform no substantive mutation and leave the pin to ordinary stale/recovery handling; never reclassify the won claim as CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED or NO_ALLOCATION.

liveness_rule.effective_signal: Use the newest durable signal attributable to the owning worker/job: pin/claim STARTED, run checkpoint, worker heartbeat, material checkpoint, or RETURN. Barrier entrant/RELEASE receipts are timing evidence only and do not create an owner before a pin exists.
liveness_rule.long_expiry_compatibility: Historical expires_at values longer than 10 minutes are not sufficient evidence of active work. If no newer durable signal exists for >=10 minutes and retry/recovery is safe, the job is recovery-eligible even when an old expires_at timestamp is still in the future.
liveness_rule.new_pin_default: New pins/claim receipts SHOULD declare expires_at approximately 10 minutes after claimed_at. Continued liveness is demonstrated by durable heartbeat/checkpoint signals rather than by a long silent lease.

generation_rule.initial: If no pin exists and no live temporary legacy owner exists, next generation is 1.
generation_rule.active: The highest generation owns execution while it has no terminal return and its newest durable signal is younger than the recovery cutoff.
generation_rule.recovery: If the highest generation has no terminal return, no newer durable signal for >=10 minutes, and retry/recovery is safe, every recovery contender derives generation + 1 and races on that exact next-generation path. The new pin references predecessor lineage and recovery basis.
generation_rule.immutability: Pin generation files are append-only and are never updated in place. Recovery creates the next generation instead of overwriting predecessor evidence.

legacy_bridge.rule: For jobs with no pins yet, legacy claims remain readable. Derive at most one temporary owner by earliest claimed_at then lexicographic claim path. The same 10-minute latest-signal recovery cutoff applies; a historical long expires_at cannot block recovery by itself.
legacy_bridge.retirement: After terminal return or recovery migration, future attempts use deterministic pins. Historical legacy claims remain append-only evidence.

collision_receipt_rule: A loser never creates a second execution claim. It reads the winner, records bounded append-only collision evidence when possible, then immediately re-enters allocation. Collision evidence cannot grant authority.
projection_rule: Live derives one authority owner from the highest valid pin generation and overlays signal age: ACTIVE <6m, STALE_SUSPECT 6-10m, REPLACEABLE >=10m without terminal result, subject to retry safety. For explicit contention fixtures it may additionally project timing states from barrier evidence under CONTENTION_BARRIER_LIVE_PROJECTION_V1.json, but those states never override pin/return authority. Terminal return is terminal regardless of historical pins/claims/barrier receipts.
host_rule: The primitive MUST be atomic create-if-absent/CAS/transactional uniqueness on the deterministic pin path. Read-then-create on a unique per-worker filename is forbidden as an authority primitive. RELEASE uses the same atomic-create requirement for timing coordination but remains non-authoritative.
required_canaries: 2 contenders -> exactly 1 pin winner and loser re-entry
5 contenders -> exactly 1 pin winner and loser re-entry
silent owner >=10m -> exactly 1 next-generation recovery winner with predecessor lineage
heartbeat younger than 10m -> no recovery takeover
multiple legacy claims -> exactly 1 temporary owner plus collision evidence
terminal return -> no new pin generation
explicit 2-worker barrier -> 2 distinct entrants -> one no-authority RELEASE -> exactly 1 pin winner + one collision loser with no loser claim
explicit barrier timeout without quorum -> no RELEASE, no pin attempt, timeout receipt + REENTER_ALLOCATION
ordinary portfolio job without explicit barrier metadata -> unchanged direct deterministic pin race
non_promotion: Passing or binding this canary mode does not make production /w operational and does not imply Current, Human Accepted or Served.
